Class AItem

java.lang.Object
edu.cnu.mdi.item.AItem
All Implemented Interfaces:
IFeedbackProvider, IDrawable, EventListener
Direct Known Subclasses:
AMapItem, LineItem, PathBasedItem, PointItem
public abstract class AItem extends Object implements IDrawable, IFeedbackProvider
Abstract base class for all interactive graphical items rendered on an IContainer.

Role in the MDI item model

An AItem is the fundamental unit of interactive content in MDI. It lives on a Layer, which in turn belongs to an IContainer. Items are drawn by the container's rendering pipeline, hit-tested by the interaction layer, and can be dragged, resized, rotated, selected, or deleted according to a set of independently-controllable behavior flags.

Drawing pipeline

The public entry point for drawing is draw(Graphics2D, IContainer), which is called by the container. Subclasses must not override draw; instead they implement the two abstract methods:

  • drawItem(Graphics2D, IContainer) — performs the actual rendering of the item's geometry.
  • shouldDraw(Graphics2D, IContainer) — returns true if the item should be drawn at all (e.g. it intersects the visible area).

Behavior flags and the lock

Each interactive behavior (dragging, resizing, rotating, deleting) is individually controlled by a boolean flag. However, the _locked flag is a master override: when true it suppresses dragging, resizing, rotating, and deleting regardless of the individual flags. Locking does not suppress visibility or selection display.

Items are locked by default (_locked = true). Call setLocked(false) or supply LOCKED=false in the constructor key-value pairs to make an item interactive.

Property-based construction

The constructor accepts an optional varargs list of alternating PropertyUtils key/value pairs. These are parsed and applied by applyProperties(Properties), which covers behavior flags, style attributes, and display name. Subclasses that need geometry parameters should override applyGeometryProperties(Properties).

Geometry

AItem provides three geometry fields that subclasses may use:

  • _path — a world-coordinate Path2D.Double for polygon-like items.
  • _line — a world-coordinate Line2D.Double for line items.
  • _focus — a world-coordinate Point2D.Double that represents the item's conceptual center.

Modification lifecycle

  1. setModification(ItemModification) — attaches the context.
  2. startModification() — classifies the operation.
  3. modify() — called repeatedly during the gesture.
  4. stopModification() — finalises, notifies, clears.

      protected boolean _resizable

  • Constructor Details

    • AItem

      public AItem(Layer layer, Object... keyVals)
      Construct an item on the given layer, optionally configuring it from property key-value pairs, and immediately register it.

      Registration adds the item to its layer (firing an ItemChangeType.ADDED event) and registers it as a feedback provider with the container's feedback control. Registration happens inside the constructor so that callers — including factory methods such as those in CreationSupport — do not need to take any extra step after construction.

      Construction-time event caveat

      Because registration fires the ADDED event before any subclass constructor body has run, a listener that immediately queries the item's geometry on ADDED will see only the state that applyProperties(Properties) has set — not any geometry a subclass sets after super() returns. In practice, MDI listeners that care about geometry wait for a subsequent draw or modification event, so this has not been a problem. If a future listener does need to read geometry on ADDED, the creation call-site should set geometry before adding the listener, or the listener should guard against uninitialized state.

      Parameters:
      layer - the layer to add this item to; must not be null
      keyVals - optional alternating PropertyUtils key/value pairs (may be empty or null)
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if layer is null

  • Method Details

    • applyProperties

      protected void applyProperties(Properties props)
      Apply a set of properties to this item's behavior flags, style, name, and geometry.

      Called from the Phase-1 constructor. May also be called later to reconfigure the item. Order: flags → name → style → geometry.

      Parameters:
      props - properties to apply; a no-op if null

    • applyStyleProperties

      protected void applyStyleProperties(Properties props)
      Apply style-related properties from props.

      Each property is applied only when the key is present; missing keys leave the current style unchanged. Subclasses that support additional style properties should override this method and call super.applyStyleProperties(props) first.

      Parameters:
      props - the properties to read; must not be null

    • applyGeometryProperties

      protected void applyGeometryProperties(Properties props)
      Apply geometry-specific properties from props.

      Default implementation is a no-op. Subclasses with geometric constructor parameters (radius, width, endpoint coordinates, etc.) should override this rather than adding constructor parameters.

      Parameters:
      props - the properties to read; never null

    • draw

      public void draw(Graphics2D g2, IContainer container)
      Draw this item onto the container.

      This is the method called by the container's rendering pipeline. Subclasses must not override it; implement drawItem(Graphics2D, IContainer) instead.

      Steps performed:

      1. Skip if _visible is false.
      2. Call shouldDraw(Graphics2D, IContainer) — skip drawItem(Graphics2D, IContainer) if false.
      3. Install any special clip from the owning BaseView.
      4. Save and restore the Stroke around drawItem(Graphics2D, IContainer).
      5. Call drawSelections(Graphics2D, IContainer) unconditionally (selected items need handles even when scrolled partially out of view).
      Specified by:
      draw in interface IDrawable
      Parameters:
      g2 - the graphics context
      container - the container being rendered

    • drawItem

      public abstract void drawItem(Graphics2D g2, IContainer container)
      Perform the actual rendering of this item's geometry.

      Called by draw(Graphics2D, IContainer) after visibility and clip setup. The stroke is saved and restored by draw, so subclasses may freely change the stroke without cleanup.

      Parameters:
      g2 - the graphics context
      container - the container being rendered

    • shouldDraw

      public abstract boolean shouldDraw(Graphics2D g2, IContainer container)
      Return true if this item should be drawn on the current frame.

      This is a secondary visibility check beyond the simple _visible flag. A typical implementation checks whether the item's screen bounds intersect the current clip rectangle.

      Parameters:
      g2 - the graphics context (may be used to read clip bounds)
      container - the container being rendered
      Returns:
      true if drawItem(Graphics2D, IContainer) should be called

    • drawSelections

      public void drawSelections(Graphics2D g2, IContainer container)
      Draw selection handles and the focus indicator for this item.

      Called unconditionally by draw(Graphics2D, IContainer) whenever the item is visible, even when shouldDraw(Graphics2D, IContainer) returned false, so handles remain visible for selected items that are partially scrolled out of view.

      When selected, draws:

      • A white oval at each selection point.
      • A yellow rotation-handle oval plus rotateIcon, if rotatable.
      • The focus indicator via focusFill(Graphics2D, IContainer).
      Parameters:
      g2 - the graphics context
      container - the container being rendered

    • setFillFocus

      public void setFillFocus(boolean fillFocus)
      Return whether the focus indicator is drawn when selected.

    • focusFill

      protected void focusFill(Graphics2D g2, IContainer container)
      Draw a small filled square at the item's focus point.

      Only drawn when getFocus() returns a non-null point. The indicator is a 6×6 pixel square filled with _FOCUSFILL.

      Parameters:
      g2 - the graphics context
      container - the container being rendered

    • contains

      public boolean contains(IContainer container, Point screenPoint)
      Test whether this item, as rendered, contains the given screen point.

      Priority order:

      1. _lastDrawnPolygon — exact hit test.
      2. getBounds(IContainer) — axis-aligned bounding rectangle.
      3. inASelectRect(IContainer, Point) — selection/rotation handle rectangles.
      Parameters:
      container - the container rendering this item
      screenPoint - the pixel point to test
      Returns:
      true if the item contains screenPoint

      public int inSelectPoint(IContainer container, Point screenPoint, boolean checkResizable)
      Return the index of the selection handle whose hit-test rectangle contains the given screen point, or -1 if none does.

      Returns -1 immediately if the item is not selected, or if checkResizable is true and the item is not resizable.

    • acceptModification

      public boolean acceptModification(GestureContext gc)
      Gives an item a final chance to accept or reject an interactive modification.

      The default implementation accepts all modifications. Subclasses may override this to enforce domain constraints after a drag, resize, or rotation gesture. For example, a map-native radar item can reject a drag that leaves a ground-based radar over water.

      This method is called near the end of the tool-handler gesture, before stopModification() clears the active modification context.

      Parameters:
      gc - the gesture context for the interaction
      Returns:
      true to keep the modified state; false to reject it

    • prepareForRemoval

      public void prepareForRemoval()
      Prepare this item for removal from its layer.

      Performs two operations:

      1. Feedback de-registration. The item unregisters itself from the container's FeedbackControl so that it is no longer polled after removal. The container reference is captured before _layer is nulled.
      2. Reference nulling. Heavyweight references are set to null to assist garbage collection and to cause fast, obvious NullPointerExceptions if the item is used after removal.

      Subclasses holding additional heavyweight references should override this method, null those fields, and call super.prepareForRemoval() either first or last.

      Specified by:
      prepareForRemoval in interface IDrawable
